standard_prerequisites.name: Root systems and structure theory of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras
standard_prerequisites.reference: Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. IV-VI; the article's own conventions at source lines 199-224
standard_prerequisites.use: Roots, coroots, the highest root theta, the invariant form normalized on long roots and d_alpha = 2/(alpha|alpha) are assumed. The dichotomy (theta|alpha) in {0,1} for alpha in R^+ different from theta, its consequence for <k theta, alpha^vee>, and the short/long root alternatives are part of the retained proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Local Weyl modules for the current algebra g[t] and their defining relations
standard_prerequisites.reference: source lines 286-315, supplied as context (Chari-Pressley; Chari-Fourier-Khandai)
standard_prerequisites.use: The excerpt carries the author's definition of W(lambda), its grading, and the relation (w2') that follows from Garland's identity. Comparing those relations with the defining families of the level-one Demazure quotient is the retained proof.

core_obligations: Show that for alpha in R^+ different from theta one has <k theta, alpha^vee> = 0 or k d_alpha, so that the relation family (dm2) is empty in D(1,k theta) and (dm1) reduces to (x^-_alpha (x) t^k) wbar_{k theta} = 0 for the short roots alpha with (theta|alpha) = 1 (source lines 427-439).
For a long root alpha with (theta|alpha) = 1, obtain the same vanishing from relation (w2') (line 440).

Identify the remaining relations with the defining relations of the local Weyl module W(k theta) and conclude that the displayed list is a complete set of defining relations for the graded g[t]-module D(1,k theta) generated by wbar_{k theta} (line 441).
proof_roadmap: Recall that (theta|alpha) is 0 or 1 for every positive root alpha different from theta, hence <k theta, alpha^vee> is 0 or k d_alpha.
Conclude that the second relation family (dm2) of the level-one Demazure definition never occurs for the weight k theta.
Rewrite the first family (dm1) as (x^-_alpha (x) t^k) wbar_{k theta} = 0 over the short roots with (theta|alpha) = 1, and extend it to long roots by (w2').
Observe that all remaining relations are exactly the defining relations of W(k theta), so the presentation is complete.
difficulty_reason: The claim is a complete presentation of the level-one Demazure module D(1,k theta), so the proof has to match the two relation families (dm1) and (dm2) that define the level-one Demazure quotient (source lines 381-393) against the relations of the local Weyl module W(k theta). The decisive step is the root-system dichotomy <k theta, alpha^vee> = 0 or k d_alpha for alpha in R^+ different from theta (lines 427-429), which kills the whole family (dm2) and reduces (dm1) to the short roots with (theta|alpha) = 1. The remaining long-root case is not formal either: it uses the relation (w2') obtained from Garland's identity (line 440). The resulting list is exactly the presentation later sections use for D(1,k theta), so it cannot be replaced by a citation to the definition of the local Weyl module.
